model_annotations.Bulgarian:
Figure 4 illustrates the mean absolute values of hidden state means at different layers before and after applying a gating mechanism, with the baseline and post-gating values noted as being similar.

The horizontal axis (X-axis) is labeled "Layer" and represents discrete integer values ranging from 0 to 20, with tick marks and labels at intervals of 5 (i.e., at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20).

The vertical axis (Y-axis) is labeled "Abs. Mean" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 4. The axis has tick marks and labels at intervals of 1 (i.e., at 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4).

The plot contains three distinct lines, each with a different color and corresponding label:
- A green line, labeled "Hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71", starts at a value of approximately 0.71 at Layer 0 and remains nearly flat across layers 0 to 20, with minor fluctuations, ending at approximately 0.71 at Layer 20.
- A blue line, labeled "Hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05", starts at a value of approximately 0.05 at Layer 0 and remains nearly flat across layers 0 to 20, with minor fluctuations, ending at approximately 0.05 at Layer 20.
- A red line, labeled "Hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04", starts at a value of approximately 0.04 at Layer 0 and remains nearly flat across layers 0 to 20, with minor fluctuations, ending at approximately 0.04 at Layer 20.

All three lines are solid and do not use markers. The green line is consistently above the blue and red lines across all layers shown.
model_annotations.Chinese: Figure 4 displays the mean absolute values of hidden state means across different layers, comparing the values before and after applying a gating mechanism. The x-axis represents the layer number, ranging from 0 to 20, with uniform numerical intervals of 5. The y-axis represents the absolute mean value, scaled linearly from 0 to 4. The chart contains three lines: a green line with circular markers representing the hidden state mean before the gate, averaging 0.71; a blue line with triangular markers representing the hidden state mean after the gate, averaging 0.05; and a black line with square markers representing the hidden state mean of the baseline, averaging 0.04. All three lines begin near the origin, with the green line showing a gradual increase to a peak value of approximately 3.8 at layer 20, while the blue and black lines remain relatively flat near zero throughout the layer range.

Mean,” is also linear and ranges from 0 to 4, with tick marks at intervals of 1. The plot contains three lines: a green line with circular markers representing “Hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71,” which remains low and nearly flat throughout; a blue line with triangular markers representing “Hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05,” which starts near zero and rises slightly to approximately 0.25 by layer 20; and a black line with square markers representing “Hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04,” which remains nearly flat near zero across all layers.
model_annotations.German: Figure 4 displays the mean absolute values of hidden state means across layers, comparing the state before gating, after gating, and the baseline, with all three values being similar. The x-axis represents the layer number, ranging from 0 to 25 in integer increments, and is labeled “Layer”. The y-axis represents the absolute mean value, ranging from 0 to 4, with tick marks at regular intervals of 1. The blue line, labeled “hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71”, starts at approximately 0.71 and remains nearly flat until layer 20, where it sharply increases to approximately 4. The green line, labeled “hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05”, starts at approximately 0.05 and remains nearly flat across all layers. The orange line, labeled “hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04”, starts at approximately 0.04 and remains nearly flat across all layers.
